sections.title: CAROLINAS/MID-ATLANTIC STATES/DELMARVA/PA
sections.text: THE BRUNT OF A BROAD/DEEP LONGWAVE TROUGH WILL GENERALLY SHIFT EAST-NORTHEASTWARD FROM THE LOWER/MIDDLE MS RIVER VALLEY TOWARD THE OH VALLEY/APPALACHIANS THROUGH TONIGHT. INITIALLY TODAY...SEVERE POTENTIAL WILL BE FOCUSED ACROSS AREAS SUCH AS THE COASTAL CAROLINAS...WHERE STRONG/MODESTLY VEERING LOW/MID TROPOSPHERIC FLOW WILL COINCIDE WITH AN INLAND DEVELOPING MOIST/UNSTABLE NEAR-COASTAL AIRMASS. IN THIS CASE...CONCERN EXISTS INTO THE MIDDAY HOURS FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF A TORNADO OR TWO AS WELL AS DAMAGING WINDS MAINLY FOR COASTAL AREAS. INTO THE UPSTATE CAROLINAS/MID-ATLANTIC REGION AND A BIT LATER TODAY...POTENTIAL FOR STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE THIS AFTERNOON/TONIGHT AS A MOIST INFLUX CONTINUES AND THE PARENT CYCLONE UNDERGOES A DEEPENING PHASE/BECOMES NEGATIVELY TILTED. WHILE A SHALLOW NEAR-SURFACE STABLE LAYER MAY TEND TO PERSIST ACROSS THE REGION AND DESTABILIZATION SHOULD OTHERWISE REMAIN MODEST...PRONOUNCED HEIGHT FALLS/DPVA AND DRAMATICALLY STRENGTHENING DEEP LAYER SOUTH-SOUTHWESTERLY FLOW PROVIDES CONCERN FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A LOW-TOPPED/FAST-MOVING CONVECTIVE LINE IN VICINITY OF AN EAST-NORTHEASTWARD ACCELERATING COLD FRONT FROM

sections.title: OH VALLEY TO THE APPALACHIANS
sections.text: WITHIN THE UPPER JET EXIT REGION...LOW-TOPPED STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE REGION IN VICINITY OF THE SURFACE COLD/OCCLUDED FRONT. WHILE BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE/INSTABILITY WILL BE MODEST...STEEP LOW/MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND CONSIDERABLE VERTICAL SHEAR MAY YIELD AN AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING RISK FOR SEVERE HAIL/WIND AND PERHAPS EVEN A BRIEF TORNADO. UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE DEGREE OF DESTABILIZATION PRECLUDES A FURTHER EXPANSION OF THE CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK AT THIS TIME.

sections.title: SOUTH FL TODAY
sections.text: SCATTERED TSTMS AND A POSSIBLE SEVERE THREAT IN THE FORM OF DAMAGING WINDS AND/OR A TORNADO MAY PERSIST THROUGH THE MORNING/MIDDAY HOURS ACROSS SOUTH FL. WITH TIME...WEAKENING/VEERING LOW-LEVEL FLOW AND EVENTUAL FRONTAL PASSAGE SHOULD LEAD TO AN INCREASINGLY MARGINAL/ISOLATED SEVERE POTENTIAL THROUGH THE DAY. ..GUYER/GARNER.. 10/19/2011

sections.title: NC NWD INTO THE MID ATLANTIC THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: A SURFACE LOW IN ERN TN/KY WILL MOVE NWD TO OHIO AND DEEPEN/OCCLUDE BY TONIGHT...AS A 90-110 KT MIDLEVEL SPEED MAX ROTATES NEWD FROM THE LOWER MS VALLEY TO THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS AND MID ATLANTIC. A TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL PROGRESS EWD TO THE SE ATLANTIC COAST THIS AFTERNOON...AND ACROSS THE MID ATLANTIC EARLY TONIGHT. IN ADVANCE OF THE COLD FRONT...A WARM FRONT WILL MOVE NWD/NWWD TO CENTRAL NC AND THE DELMARVA THIS AFTERNOON IN CONJUNCTION WITH A WEAKER/SECONDARY SURFACE LOW MOVING NNEWD FROM THE GA/SC BORDER. A MOIST MARITIME AIR MASS /BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS OF 68-72 F/ WILL SPREAD INLAND WITH THE WARM FRONT...AND CLOUD BREAKS FROM ERN NC INTO SE VA WILL ALLOW WARM SECTOR TEMPERATURES TO POTENTIALLY REACH 75-80 F. MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL NOT BE STEEP...BUT THE SURFACE HEATING/MOISTENING WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 500-1500 J/KG. THERE WILL BE SOME RISK FOR EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS AND AN ISOLATED TORNADO INVOF THE NC COAST THIS MORNING WITH AN INITIAL SW-NE BAND OF CONVECTION IN A STRONG LOW-LEVEL SHEAR ENVIRONMENT. THIS CONVECTION IS EXPECTED TO MOVE AWAY FROM ERN NC BY ABOUT MIDDAY-EARLY AFTERNOON. THE NEXT FOCUS FOR CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON WIL

sections.title: SE FL THIS MORNING
sections.text: LOW-LEVEL WINDS HAVE CONTINUED TO VEER TO SWLY THE PAST SEVERAL HOURS...AND THE PRE-FRONTAL FOCUS FOR THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT WILL SHIFT OFF THE SE FL COAST BY ABOUT MIDDAY. IN THE MEANTIME...AN ISOLATED STRONG GUST WILL BE THE MAIN CONCERN AROUND MIAMI AND THE UPPER KEYS. ..THOMPSON/BOTHWELL.. 10/19/2011
